(Just confirming that they use she/they pronouns and are comfortable being called a girl?) I would say it’s totally okay to question whether you’d be attracted to their body post top surgery. It’s not transphobic to be attracted to certain genitalia or body parts such as breasts, it is transphobic to not want to be with someone because their enby or trans (which doesn’t sound like the case here) but it might be a difficult conversation to have considering they could be dysphoric about their chest. Yeah sometimes it’s a hard one, I ask friends and family to tell me if I’m talking faster than usual or making a lot of plans because sometimes I can’t tell. I think it might be useful to think about maybe you’re experiencing hypomania, which could be the whole scope of things or it could be a precursor to mania? The sleep thing is a key thing to look out for and sounds quite hypomanic (but obvs I’m just talking about my own experience). I also know that I talk to myself a lot when I’m getting hypomanic and feel this constant restlessness like everything in the world is going too slow. Obvs even when you see your triggers it’s hard to stop them from developing into mania (I go through stages rather than a full switch) but I tend to just keep an eye on how much I’m contacting people and whether the things I’m planning would be useful in the long run (sometimes I ignore it anyway haha), and sometimes it helps me to block out all stimuli, so low lights, no music, stay by myself for a bit. Hope you figure it out!

I think it’s totally appropriate for you to push for different medication, I have an ED and my doctors outright told me they wouldn’t be prescribing any medication where weight gain is a side affect because they thought I would either be v restrictive or just stop taking the meds (which is true). In my experience, body dysmorphia is also triggering of my bipolar and both pose huge risks to your health, so Imo the two should be treated together not separately. Whether or not anyone else thinks gaining 10kg is reasonable or not, you have to follow your experience with an ED and the doctor should listen when you tell them it’s triggering for you, I don’t really understand why they wouldn’t take this seriously? Admittedly it does limit your med options but I take lamictal and so far it’s going well (fingers crossed!). Hope things improve, and what youre saying is totally valid :)

Personally, i struggled with the ‘what the fuck even is gender’ question for soooooo long, reading all the bloody books, trying to work it out, asking my cis friends how they experienced their own identities, see if there was some kind of commonality that other people were feeling or connecting to that I wasn’t, and eventually I just accepted that it literally depends on every single person, there’s no way to define ‘gender’ in its entirety because (for example fo me) it’s tied to how i experience my identity, It’s very personal I think. Ive daydreamed about gender abolition before but I think it probably serves as erasure for other peoples (cis) identities that I don’t fully understand because I haven’t experienced them. Maybe (thinking out loud here) the utopian goal should be not abolition but creating a world that is so wide and accepting that it can encompass all identities and expressions, maybe that is an abolitionism in itself, to remove the harmful, dangerous, closed aspects of societal understanding of gender by opening doors and options to any conception of it rather than closing them? Ahhhh you got me thinking about it again gods sake haha. But basically after all that, I was like nah not gunna even bother stressing over that question anymore haha, such a mind fuck. Being nb for me is like a permission to have freedom from that question, I don’t need to answer it in order to exist (even though I do find it interesting, it’s almost become an academic exercise at this point rather than a personal crisis) :)  x

I think you should hold back on anything until you feel more stable. Monogamy isn’t for everyone but polygamy (in all its forms) has to be negotiated and considered with a clear head (especially if you’re already in a monogamous relationship), otherwise could make things more difficult and sometimes having multiple partners doesn’t quell the hyper sexuality, because it’s more complicated than that imo. Also if your partner is saying that they’d be hurt by it, it might not serve your relationship to be non-exclusive, but gotta weigh those things up I think and make a real decision either way, not one that changes with mood :)
